s1.note: No student requirement — open to Amazon customers; US shipping addresses only for trade-ins.

s2.note: Payment is an Amazon.com gift card, NOT cash — store credit only. Trade-in value varies per book by demand, condition, and market value.

s3.note: Gift card deposited after book is received and verified by a third-party merchant.

s4.note: No fixed $150 figure on official sources — the $150 claim is unsupported.

payout_quote: Amazon.com today announced the new Textbooks Trade-In program, which allows customers to exchange used textbooks in return for an Amazon.com gift card. ... Students just visit www.amazon.com/tradeinbooks, and search for the books they want to trade. Then students can print a pre-paid shipping label and drop the package in the mail. Once the book is received and verified by a third-party merchant, an Amazon.com gift card will be deposited into the student's Amazon.com account.
timing: Amazon.com gift card deposited into your account after the book is received and verified by a third-party merchant.
eligibility: Amazon customers; trade-ins must ship from the United States to a US address.
catches: Paid in Amazon gift card only — not cash; it locks your money into Amazon.
Trade-in value varies per book (demand, condition, edition) — the $150 headline is unsupported.
Books must pass Amazon's condition inspection or the offer is adjusted/rejected.
Not all books are eligible — outdated editions and damaged books may get no offer.

weasel_words.quote: No fixed dollar amount in official sources — '$150' is an unsupported headline; trade-in values are per-book.

steps: Go to https://www.amazon.com/tradeinbooks and search your textbook by ISBN, title, or author.
Check whether the book is eligible — Amazon displays the trade-in value for eligible books.
Accept the trade-in value and complete the trade-in checkout to generate a prepaid shipping label.
Package the book securely and ship it using the prepaid label.
Amazon's third-party merchant receives and verifies the book's condition.
An Amazon.com gift card for the agreed value is deposited into your Amazon account.
biggest_catch: You get paid in Amazon gift card, not cash — and the amount is whatever Amazon offers for your specific book, not $150.
notes: Verified on Amazon's official announcement and trade-in page. Route's $150 claim unsupported. Frame as store-credit conversion, never cash income.
